title: Module 9 Interpretation Check
intro: Each item gives you a short research situation. Decide what the evidence supports.

items.q: Twelve students are tested before and after a workshop. The mean change is +3.0, and the SD of the difference scores is 4.2. What is the estimated standard error?
items.why: sMD = 4.2 divided by the square root of 12 = 1.21.

items.q: What is t, and what are the degrees of freedom?
items.why: t = 3.0/1.212 = 2.474 with df = 12 minus 1 = 11. The critical t at .05 two-tailed is 2.201, so the result is significant (p = .031).

items.q: The 95 percent CI for the mean change is 3.0 plus or minus 2.201(1.212). What are the limits?
items.why: 2.201 times 1.212 = 2.67. The CI excludes zero, matching the significant test.

items.q: A researcher analyzes pre and post scores from the same 30 patients using an independent-measures t test. What is the main problem?
o: The two sets of scores are dependent, so the independent test ignores the pairing and gives the wrong error term
items.why: Use the related-samples test on the difference scores.
